decisions.rationale: Basis: ops-reconciler-loop6 on a scratch copy (reconciler-r6/lab) of the frozen export at 18ac2ad0 (lab.json sha256 583b8964, README.md bfd2a0b4, tests/lab.mjs a5228f92, tests/behavior.mjs f5f793a4, tests/service_behavior.py 68cbaf01, tests/setup_python.mjs 06b667dc); npm run setup in tests (npm ci, then a Python 3.14.6 .venv with the 14 pins), Node v24.2.0, /bin/bash 3.2.57, macOS arm64, TMPDIR inside the reconciler folder; every run under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result and count lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's solution passes 26/26 and its lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt; only its reviews/app/main.py was written by the reconciler (from README phase 4 and the service-to-service page), the other files are the SME critic's solution (sme-recheck6/sol), which no finding contests. The S38 checkpoint state (that solution with the starter ci.yml and the starter's phase-7 sections) passes exactly 9-19 and 23-26 (15/26). 20 variants of the solution, most one edit (the inline-ValueError and catch-all ones make two), and one of the starter (starter-url-only) (reconciler-r6/variants, variants-out.txt and the runs folder). The required tests/lab.mjs, tests/behavior.mjs and tests/service_behavior.py changes below were prototyped in a separate copy (reconciler-r6/proto, proto.diff, proto-out.txt, proto-out2.txt, proto-out3.txt); the setup_python.mjs message and the README line 119 edit were not prototyped (text changes, recheck by reading). With the prototype the solution still passes 26/26, both summaries are unchanged, the checkpoint still passes the same 15 with its messages unchanged, and the only starter message that changes is test 26's. The prototype is evidence of feasibility, not the fix; the author implements it. Not run: Windows, Linux, a real docker, a GitHub runner, a real Python 3.10 or 3.15, an interpreter with no matching wheel; the critics' variant ci-raw-fold-echo was not run (ci-raw-fold and ci-raw-two-halves were). No web page was re-retrieved; claims resting on GitHub, Starlette or pip pages cite the critics' dated retrievals. Ruling principle (loop 5C instruction): earlier shape lists are evidence of plausible learner shapes, not an allowlist; each finding is judged on whether behaviour matches the README objective, whether a plausible correct solution is falsely rejected or a real leak falsely accepted, and whether each message is true and non-revealing. Valid, low. Reproduced on the export: the inline httpx.Timeout(connect=2.0, read=3.0) variant scores 23/26 and tests 24-26 name the ValueError but end 'call the api with httpx, as the starter does', 'make the call and send the caller's token on it' and 'make the call to the shop api with httpx'; the hard-coded http://api:8080 variant scores 23/26 and names the URL but ends the same way. The learner has written the call in both, so the endings are untrue guidance, and the loop-5 required change (no-call wording only when no HTTPX request was made and nothing was raised) is not met. Required minimal change (one change covers ops-edu-r6-01, ops-sme-r6-02 and the open ops-edu-r5-02): (1) service_behavior.py keeps the escaped exception in every case, including the catch-all fallback (lines 89-93), for example result['raised'] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300] set before the fallback rerun, so lab.mjs can name it; the fallback itself and its status stay. (2) In lab.mjs, the three no-call branches (lines 241, 255, 276) choose their ending by what the scenario recorded, in this precedence: if the scenario recorded any outgoing request and none to API_BASE_URL, name the URL called and say to build the call's URL from API_BASE_URL; in test 26 that branch prints no status and no exception text for the failure scenario (the stand-in's simulated timeout must not be reported as the service's answer to a call that may carry no limit); otherwise, if it recorded zero outgoing requests and an exception, say once that the handler raised <Type>: <text> before it called the shop api and to fix that error (name the exception once: today statusText already prints it, so drop it from one place); only when nothing was requested and nothing was raised keep the existing 'make the call' wording. No hint of any constructor form (ops-edu-11). Prototype trap found by the reconciler: an ordering that checks the recorded exception first is wrong; the starter with only the URL hard-coded (variants/starter-url-only) then reports the stand-in's ReadTimeout as raised 'before it called the shop api'. Recheck: svc-inline-timeout-valueerror and svc-catchall-inline-valueerror fail 24-26 naming the ValueError once with no 'make the call' advice; svc-hardcoded-url and starter-url-only fail 24-26 with the URL and the API_BASE_URL ending and, in test 26, no status and no exception text; the shipped starter and checkpoint messages of 24 and 25 are unchanged; the solution passes 26/26.

Valid, medium. Reproduced: the shipped starter's test 26 message reports, in the worksheet item's own scenario, that the service answered 500 because the stand-in's ReadTimeout escaped, from a call that passes timeout=None. The value is not repeated here. The same holds for a call with no timeout argument: it runs with HTTPX's default limits, and the stand-in's timeout is then also a description of what that client does, which is the item beside it. Not a false accept or reject: with timeout=None or no timeout argument and correct handlers, test 26 passes and test 24 fails (variants svc-timeout-none-handlers-ok, svc-no-timeout-argument, 25/26). Required minimal change, in the message only (pass/fail unchanged): in reviews-error-mapping, when a timeout scenario's status is not accepted and the call recorded in that scenario has no limit for that phase (read for the read-timeout case, connect for the connect-timeout case) or carries only HTTPX's default (the same unset test test 24 uses: all four limits none, or all four 5), return one neutral message that says only that test 26 reports the detail of its timeout cases only for a call that carries the connect and read limits test 24 asks for (not that they are 'judged' only then: with handlers such a call already passes test 26). It must not describe what any client does against an api that sends nothing, must not name the stand-in's exception, and must not state a status. The refused case is unchanged. In the export, the same untrue report also reaches test 26 through the no-call branch when the call goes to another URL (starter-url-only prints the ReadTimeout there); the ops-edu-r6-01 precedence removes that. Prototyped: the starter's test 26 becomes 'test 26 reports the detail of its timeout cases only for a call that carries the connect and read limits test 24 asks for: finish test 24, then run again' and no other starter message changes; svc-limits-ok-no-handlers (limits set, no handlers) keeps its true ReadTimeout message. Recheck: sweep every starter and checkpoint message again for a stated or ruled-out option of any worksheet item (this also closes ops-edu-r5-04 and ops-edu-11); svc-timeout-none-handlers-ok and svc-no-timeout-argument stay 25/26; expected/starter-summary.txt unchanged.

This replaces the value and value-plus-newline forms (both are covered). Prototyped: all four variants then fail only test 7 with the existing base64-encoded message; ci-b64-single-wrapped still fails; the solution, the ::add-mask:: of a derived value (ci-addmask-derived) and the starter and checkpoint runs are unchanged. Recheck: the four variants fail only test 7; the README login form, the passing add-mask form and both summaries are unchanged.
